facts.value: Theory of the Firm and the Household

Covers issues like regulation, game theory, welfare effects of government-induced price distortions, and the theory of market failures. Provides students with modern tools while enabling them to understand and work with scholarly articles in areas such as public finance and industrial organization.

Introduces basic concepts and key tools central to understanding macroeconomic issues, ranging from short-term economic fluctuations to long-term growth. Students learn to apply mathematical tools for analyzing model economies and developing policy recommendations.

Introduces methods behind the empirical analysis of micro- and macro-data encountered in cross-sectional and time series studies. Application demonstrated with real data examples. Requires familiarity with linear regression models and elementary econometrics.

Designed to provide a solid understanding of theoretical concepts related to capital markets and equip students with practical application skills. Discusses utility theory, modern portfolio theory, asset pricing models, and option pricing theory.
